technology_name: Evaluating Road Safety Using Surrogate Measures on Two-Lane Highways
institution: KSCSTE - National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC)
problem_solved: High accident rates of motorized two-wheelers (MTWs) on congested corridors and the lack of empirical metrics to quantify near-miss collision risks before crashes occur.
description: An operational and safety evaluation of dedicated, inclusive Motorized Two-Wheeler (MTW) lanes marked within standard two-lane highway carriageways (pilot-tested on the Muvattupuzha-Vengalloor stretch). The framework utilizes drone videography and GIS risk mapping paired with advanced surrogate safety metrics—specifically Time-to-Collision (TTC)—to isolate spatial conflict points (such as the Kothamangalam junction) where car-to-MTW interactions reach a critical average TTC threshold of 1.34 seconds.
applications:
• Highway design modification guidelines and smart corridor planning

• Automated traffic conflict monitoring software for urban surveillance cameras

• Municipal traffic enforcement mapping and junction geometric restructuring

• Advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) trained on mixed-traffic vehicle behaviors
